chapter: Early life and New York scene
title: Nick's, 52nd Street and Kelly's Stables as a teenager
summary: Chicago style and Nick's were the big influence; kids sat by the bandstand, and he saw Coleman Hawkins at Kelly's.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, when we started out playing, the emphasis among the group of musicians around Scarsdale and Westchester was on the Chicago style and the big influence was the music at Nick's, which was the place in New York.
Did you all get down there? I don't remember now the policy of letting kids in under age or not. What did they do?

I don't remember. I remember when I was 13 and mostly on Sunday afternoons and they would let, they had, at that time they had a dance floor and they had three pianos lined up, three upright pianos in front of the bandstand. I remember that, yeah. And they used to let us kids sit inside the piano and actually sit on the edge of the bandstand. And I'd be sitting there like two feet from Brad Gowan's feet and peewee. And I think Chelsea Qualey was on trumpet at that time and sometimes Hackett. So that was, they were very nice about letting kids in, you know, because they knew we were young musicians, you know, and wanted to learn. In fact, I remember, I guess I was 14 or 15, going into places on 52nd Street and they didn't bother me. By yourself? Your parents? Anybody take care of them?

Kids, it seems amazing now, but I remember a thrilling time going into Kelly's stables and sitting at a front table, right in front of the bandstand. And the band was playing and Coleman Hawkins walks up to the bandstand and picks up the tenor and one of the fellows in the band says, what do you want to play, Hawk? And he says, body, one, two. And he starts playing. And they didn't bother us.
